examples.en: The government changed its stance under the opposition's fierce attack.
Our team launched a fierce attack in the second half.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 맹공을 잘 막아 냈어요.
examples.en: We held off the other team's fierce attack well.
The candidates attacked each other fiercely.
After the press conference, harsh attacks poured onto the politician.

examples.ko: 신제품이 경쟁사의 맹공 속에서도 잘 팔렸어요.
examples.en: The new product sold well even amid the rival's aggressive push.

explain: 스포츠 경기나 정치 뉴스에서 공격이나 비판을 강하게 몰아붙일 때 써요. '맹공을 퍼붓다/가하다/받다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: The opposition poured fierce attacks on the government's policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 시간에 강하게 많이 공격하거나 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when attacking or criticizing a lot and strongly in a short time.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 상대 골대에 맹공을 가했어요.
phrases.en: Our team launched a fierce attack on the opponent's goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '퍼붓다'보다 조금 딱딱해서 뉴스나 기사에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more formal than '퍼붓다', often seen in news and articles.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 거짓 광고 때문에 맹공을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The company came under fierce attack because of its false advertising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공격하는 쪽이 아니라 공격을 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one being attacked, not the attacker.

explain_en: Fierce, concentrated attack, as in sports or battle (우리 팀은 경기 시작부터 상대 골대를 향해 맹공을 펼쳤어요.) It is used in sports and political news when attacks or criticism are pressed hard. Learn it as a set phrase: '맹공을 퍼붓다/가하다/받다'.

examples.en: The suspect was sighted at the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 이 근처에서 큰 새가 자주 목격돼요.
examples.en: A large bird is often seen around here.
Citizens witnessed the criminal running away.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 하늘에서 이상한 불빛이 목격됐다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a strange light was seen in the sky last night.

examples.ko: 곰이 마을에서 목격되면 바로 신고해야 해요.
examples.en: If a bear is spotted in the village, you must report it right away.

examples.ko: 범인이 목격된 장소를 경찰이 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are investigating the place where the culprit was sighted.

explain: 누군가의 눈에 띄었다는 사실을 객관적으로 전할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 사건, 사고, 동물, 이상한 현상처럼 눈에 띄는 일이 대상이에요. 직접 본 사람 입장에서는 '목격하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I saw the accident myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 본 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person who saw it as the subject.

phrases.en: The witness told the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이나 사고를 직접 본 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who saw an incident or accident.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 그 뒤로 목격되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That person hasn't been seen since.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 아무도 보지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means nobody has seen them.

explain_en: News uses it to report neutrally that something was seen by someone. The subject is usually an incident, an accident, an animal, or an odd phenomenon. From the viewpoint of the person who saw it, say 목격하다.

examples.ko: 역사책에서 마을 사람들의 몰살 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about the massacre of a village in a history book.

examples.ko: 그 전쟁은 한 민족의 몰살로 이어졌어요.
examples.en: That war led to the wiping out of a people.

examples.ko: 영화 속에서 병사들이 몰살 직전까지 갔어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the soldiers came close to being wiped out.
People ran away to avoid being slaughtered.

examples.ko: 공룡의 몰살은 큰 운석 때문이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the dinosaurs' wiping out was caused by a huge meteorite.
A terrible massacre happens in this story.

explain: '몰살'은 한 사람이 아니라 한 무리가 통째로 죽는 큰 사건에 써요. '전멸'은 군대나 팀이 모두 없어지는 것이라, 게임에서 팀이 다 죽어도 '전멸했다'고 말해요. 실제 사건을 말할 땐 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 역사에는 집단 몰살의 슬픈 기록이 있어요.
phrases.en: History has sad records of mass killings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 무리가 통째로 죽은 큰 사건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for large events where a whole group was killed.

phrases.en: The villagers were wiped out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당한 쪽에서 말할 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used from the victims' side.

phrases.en: Our team was wiped out in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 팀이 모두 없어질 때 쓰고, 게임에서는 가볍게도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a unit or team is entirely lost; also casual in games.

explain_en: 몰살 is for a big event in which a whole group dies, not just one person. 전멸 is when an army or team is entirely lost, and in games a team that all dies can be said to be 전멸했다. For real events, 몰살 is a heavy word.

examples.en: The police released a composite sketch of the suspect.
I heard the sketch looks a lot like the real face.
It took a long time to make the composite sketch.

examples.ko: 영화에서 짧은 장면을 이어 붙이는 몽타주 기법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned the montage technique of joining short scenes in film.
The composite picture was distributed nationwide.

examples.ko: 이 뮤직비디오는 여러 장면을 몽타주로 엮었어요.
examples.en: This music video weaves many scenes together as a montage.

explain: 영화에서 짧은 장면을 이어 붙이는 편집 기법을 말해요. 한국어에서는 목격자의 설명으로 만든 용의자 얼굴 그림이나 사진도 '몽타주'라고 하는데, 영어로는 보통 'composite sketch'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 '몽타주를 공개하다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The police released the suspect's composite sketch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 흔한 짝말로, 용의자 얼굴 그림을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common news collocation, for releasing a suspect's face drawing.

phrases.en: They drew a composite sketch based on the witness's description.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 설명을 듣고 얼굴을 그림으로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a face is drawn based on someone's description.

phrases.example: 이 영화는 마지막 몽타주 장면이 멋있어요.
phrases.en: The final montage scene in this movie is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범인 그림이 아니라 짧은 장면을 이어 붙이는 영화 편집 기법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the film editing technique, not the suspect sketch.

explain_en: It refers to the film-editing technique of joining short scenes. In Korean, 몽타주 also means a suspect's face drawn or pieced together from a witness's description, which English usually calls a 'composite sketch'. In news it often appears as '몽타주를 공개하다'.

en: to be merciless; to be cruel; to be ruthless

examples.ko: 무자비하다는 평가를 받은 사장이 결국 물러났어요.
examples.en: The boss who was called ruthless eventually stepped down.
That coach is too merciless toward the players.
The brutal heat has continued for a week now.
Time passes mercilessly in the same way for everyone.

examples.ko: 경쟁이 너무 무자비해서 지칠 때가 있어요.
examples.en: The competition is so ruthless that I sometimes get worn out.
I'm glad I met a boss who isn't ruthless.

explain: '잔인하다'는 끔찍하게 아프게 하는 행동에 쓰고, '무자비하다'는 사정을 봐주지 않고 몰아붙이는 느낌이 강해요. 사람뿐 아니라 '무자비한 더위', '무자비한 경쟁'처럼 힘들게 하는 상황에도 비유로 써요. 반대말은 '자비롭다'예요.

phrases.en: The reporters' merciless criticism continued.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봐주지 않고 심하게 몰아붙이는 말이나 행동 앞에 '-ㄴ' 형태로 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form is used before words or actions that show no mercy.

phrases.en: The rival company cut prices ruthlessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸며서 사정을 봐주지 않고 한다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb form that adds the sense of doing something without mercy.

phrases.en: Our team leader isn't cruel; he is kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 사람이 가혹하지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say someone is not harsh.

explain_en: Showing no mercy; harsh people, weather or acts (무자비한 추위) '잔인하다' is for actions that are horrifyingly hurtful, while '무자비하다' has a strong feel of pressing on without sparing anyone's circumstances. It is used for people and also figuratively for tough situations, as in '무자비한 더위' and '무자비한 경쟁'. The opposite is '자비롭다'.

examples.en: That promise was brutally broken.
My hopes were utterly crushed, and I'm upset.
Our team lost by a crushing margin.
The beautiful forest was mercilessly cut down.
I was ruthlessly betrayed by someone I trusted.
His dream was cruelly trampled.

explain: 깨지다, 무너지다, 짓밟히다, 지다처럼 나쁜 일을 당하는 말과 잘 어울려요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고, 안타깝고 끔찍하다는 느낌이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: The dream was cruelly crushed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무너지다'는 기대나 계획이 깨질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '무너지다' is also used when hopes or plans fall apart.

phrases.en: The rights of weak people were brutally trampled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함부로 당하는 끔찍한 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a terrible situation where someone is mistreated.

phrases.en: Our team lost miserably in the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 지고 안타까운 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a heavy, painful loss.

explain_en: Literary/formal, cruel destruction or harm, often sad (무참히 무너졌어요) It pairs well with words about bad things happening, like 깨지다, 무너지다, 짓밟히다 and 지다. It is never used for good things and carries a feeling of pity and horror.

examples.ko: 예전에는 글을 읽지 못하는 문맹이 많았어요.
examples.en: In the past, there were many people who couldn't read.
This country's illiteracy rate has dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 할머니는 학교에 다닌 적이 없어서 문맹이셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother had never gone to school, so she was illiterate.

examples.ko: 정부가 문맹을 없애기 위해 야학을 열었어요.
examples.en: The government opened night schools to eliminate illiteracy.

examples.ko: 요즘은 글자는 읽어도 금융 문맹인 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, many people can read but are financially illiterate.

examples.ko: 문맹에서 벗어난 뒤 할아버지는 매일 신문을 읽으세요.
examples.en: Since getting out of illiteracy, my grandfather reads the newspaper every day.

explain: 글을 읽고 쓰지 못하는 상태를 말하고, 뉴스에서는 '문맹률'이라는 말로 자주 나와요. '금융 문맹', '디지털 문맹'처럼 어떤 분야를 잘 모르는 사람을 비유할 때도 써요. '컴맹'처럼 '-맹'을 붙인 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: I learned to read at night school and escaped illiteracy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 읽고 쓰지 못하는 상태에서 나아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has moved out of not being able to read or write.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 문맹 퇴치 운동을 오래 해 왔어요.
phrases.en: That country has run an anti-illiteracy campaign for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 사회 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in news and social topics.

phrases.example: 스마트폰이 어려운 어른을 디지털 문맹이라고 해요.
phrases.en: Adults who find smartphones hard are called digitally illiterate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분야를 잘 모르는 사람을 비유할 때 '문맹'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 문맹 to a field figuratively means someone who knows little about it.

explain_en: Neutral/formal term for being unable to read and write (문맹률) It describes not being able to read or write, and in the news it often appears as '문맹률' (illiteracy rate). It is also used figuratively for people who know little about a field, as in '금융 문맹' (financially illiterate) or '디지털 문맹'. There are also words like '컴맹' that use '-맹' the same way.

t90.ax: This country's illiteracy rate has dropped a lot.

examples.en: They were persecuted because of their religion.
They kept their faith even through long persecution.
They left for another country to escape persecution.

examples.ko: 역사책에서 소수 민족에 대한 박해를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read about the persecution of minorities in a history book.
As the persecution grew worse, many people fled.
He fought on to the end against persecution.

explain: 박해는 힘 있는 쪽이 약한 쪽을 괴롭힐 때 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 주로 종교, 민족, 역사 이야기에서 '박해를 받다', '박해에 시달리다'로 써요. 직장이나 학교의 괴롭힘에는 '괴롭힘'이 더 맞아요.

phrases.en: The minority group was persecuted for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박해를 받다'와 비슷하지만 억울하게 괴롭힘을 겪는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 박해를 받다 but with a stronger sense of suffering unjust treatment.

phrases.en: They suffered from persecution for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박해가 계속되어 힘들어하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when persecution continues and people suffer under it.

phrases.example: 종교적 박해를 피해 다른 나라로 갔어요.
phrases.en: They went to another country to escape religious persecution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박해의 이유가 종교일 때 쓰는 짝말로, 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for persecution because of religion, common in history.

explain_en: This is a heavy word for the powerful oppressing the weak. It is mostly used in stories about religion, ethnic groups, and history, as in '박해를 받다' (be persecuted). For bullying at work or school, '괴롭힘' fits better.

en: to be proclaimed; to be promulgated

examples.en: The new law will be promulgated next month.

examples.ko: 그 문자는 오백 년 전에 반포됐어요.
examples.en: That script was promulgated five hundred years ago.
Do you remember the day the constitution was promulgated?

examples.ko: 법이 반포되면 모든 사람이 따라야 해요.
examples.en: Once a law is promulgated, everyone has to follow it.
People were surprised after the rules were announced.
The new system was promulgated and schools were informed too.

explain: '법이 반포되다'처럼 법이나 새 제도가 주어로 나오고, 사람이 주어일 때는 '반포하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스, 역사 글, 교과서에서 만나요. 소식이 널리 알려질 때는 '알려지다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I saw the newly promulgated law on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 말로, 공식적으로 알려진 법이나 제도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies the following noun; refers to a law or system that was officially announced.

phrases.en: The new system will be announced next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반포되다'보다 쓰임이 넓어서 법이 아닌 계획이나 결과에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 반포되다; it also works for plans and results, not only laws.

phrases.example: 그 문자는 온 나라에 널리 반포됐어요.
phrases.en: That script was proclaimed widely across the whole country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 세상에 알려졌다는 뜻이고, 역사 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it was officially made known to the public; common in history writing.

explain_en: The subject is a law or a new system ('a law is promulgated'); when a person does it, use 반포하다. You will rarely hear it in conversation. It shows up in news, history writing and textbooks. For news simply becoming known, 알려지다 is much more natural.

examples.en: I only get going when the exam date gets close.
Everyone got into gear and started working.

examples.ko: 저는 발동은 느리지만 한번 시작하면 끝까지 해요.
examples.en: I am slow to get going, but once I start, I finish.
Some people take time to get going.

examples.ko: 발동도 안 걸렸는데 벌써 퇴근 시간이에요.
examples.en: I have not even got going and it is already time to leave work.
On cold mornings it is hard to get going.

explain: 일상에서는 '발동이 걸리다', '발동을 걸다'처럼 정해진 틀로 쓰고, 일이나 공부가 본격적으로 시작된 상태를 가리켜요. 뉴스에서는 '비상 조치가 발동되다'처럼 제도나 권한이 실제로 작동할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: to get into gear
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음에는 느리다가 몸과 마음이 일에 맞춰져 속도가 붙었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone starts slowly and then builds momentum once their body and mind settle into the work.

explain_en: In daily life it appears in fixed patterns like '발동이 걸리다' and '발동을 걸다', for work or study finally getting properly underway. In the news it also covers rules or powers actually taking effect, as in '비상 조치가 발동되다'.

examples.ko: 대표단의 방북이 다음 주에 예정돼 있어요.
examples.en: The delegation's visit to North Korea is scheduled for next week.

examples.ko: 이번 방북 일정은 아직 공개되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The schedule for this trip to North Korea hasn't been made public yet.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 방북 후에 기자회견을 열었어요.
examples.en: The lawmaker held a press conference after the visit to North Korea.

examples.ko: 방북 승인을 받는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to get approval to visit North Korea.
The government decided to allow a civic group to visit North Korea.

examples.ko: 방북 소식이 알려지자 뉴스마다 크게 다뤘어요.
examples.en: Once news of the trip to North Korea came out, every news program covered it prominently.

explain: 주로 뉴스와 기사에서 쓰는 말이에요. 반대로 북한 쪽 사람이 한국에 오는 것은 '방남'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '북한에 가다'라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The government announced its plan to visit North Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 북한에 갈 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the news to talk about a plan to visit North Korea.

phrases.en: Many people have applied to visit North Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북한에 가기 위해 허가를 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when asking for permission to go to North Korea.
phrases.en_equiv: to apply for a North Korea visit

phrases.en: The length of the North Korea visit is three days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북한에 머무르는 날짜를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for how long the stay in North Korea lasts.

explain_en: This word is used mainly in news and articles. The opposite, a North Korean visiting South Korea, is '방남'. In everyday talk people often just say '북한에 가다' (go to North Korea).

examples.ko: 두 회사의 병합이 다음 달에 끝나요.
examples.en: The merger of the two companies will finish next month.

examples.ko: 파일 병합은 한 번만 하면 돼요.
examples.en: You only need to merge the files once.

examples.ko: 병합 후에는 직원 수가 두 배가 되었어요.
examples.en: After the merger, the number of employees doubled.

examples.ko: 두 은행의 병합에 반대하는 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people opposed the merger of the two banks.

examples.ko: 표에서 셀 병합을 하면 제목이 가운데에 와서 예뻐져요.
examples.en: If you merge cells in a table, the title sits in the center and looks nicer.
The school's name changed because of the merger.

explain: 회사, 학교, 파일, 셀처럼 따로 있던 것을 하나로 합칠 때 써요. '합치다'는 어디에나 쓰고 '병합'은 회사나 문서, 데이터 같은 공식적이거나 기술적인 문맥에서 많이 나와요. 회사끼리 합치는 일은 '합병'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The merger of the two banks was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사끼리 하나가 되는 일에는 '합병'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For companies becoming one, 합병 is used more often.

phrases.en: Press merge cells in the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터 표에서 칸을 하나로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for joining cells into one in a computer table.

phrases.en: Save it when you finish merging the files.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합치는 작업이 끝났다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the merging work is done.

explain_en: 병합 is used when things that were separate, like companies, schools, files, or cells, become one. 합치다 works anywhere, while 병합 is common in formal or technical contexts. For companies joining together, 합병 is also used.

t90.ax: You only need to merge the files once.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 에너지를 볼모로 상대국을 압박했어요.
examples.en: That country pressured the other country by using energy as a bargaining chip.

examples.ko: 시민을 볼모 삼아 요구하는 건 옳지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not right to make demands by holding citizens hostage.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 왕자가 볼모가 되어 다른 나라에 가기도 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, a prince sometimes went to another country as a hostage.
Please don't treat the child like a pawn in your fight.

examples.ko: 볼모 신세가 된 왕자의 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read the story of a prince who became a hostage.

examples.ko: 예산이 정치 싸움의 볼모에서 겨우 풀려났어요.
examples.en: The budget was finally freed from being a pawn in the political fight.

explain: 원래는 약속을 지키게 하려고 상대 나라에 보낸 사람을 가리켰어요. 지금은 '볼모로 잡다/삼다'처럼 사람이나 일을 내세워 상대를 압박한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. '인질'과 비슷하지만 정치나 협상에서 압박하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 노조가 승객을 볼모로 삼는다는 비판이 나왔어요.
phrases.en: There was criticism that the union is using passengers as leverage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 상황을 앞세워 상대에게 압박을 주는 것을 비판적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when someone puts people or a situation forward to pressure the other side.
phrases.en_equiv: hold ~ hostage; use ~ as a bargaining chip

explain_en: It originally meant a person sent to another country as a guarantee of a promise. Today it is also widely used figuratively, as in '볼모로 잡다/삼다', for using a person or matter as leverage. It is close to '인질' but feels more tied to politics and negotiation pressure.

t90.ax: I read the story of a prince who became a hostage.

examples.en: The deputy prime minister held a press conference today.
The economic deputy prime minister's remarks were on the news.
The deputy prime minister ranks right below the prime minister.
They say a new deputy prime minister will be appointed.
The deputy prime minister and ministers attended the meeting.
There was a time for reporters to ask the deputy prime minister questions.

explain: 한국에서는 부총리가 경제나 교육 같은 부처의 장관을 함께 맡는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서는 '경제부총리'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 불러요.

phrases.en: The deputy prime minister for the economy announced a new policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서는 분야를 앞에 붙여 이렇게 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the news, the field is put in front like this.
phrases.en_equiv: deputy prime minister for the economy

phrases.en: He is the deputy prime minister and also the education minister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부총리가 장관 일을 함께 맡을 때 이렇게 소개해요.
phrases.nuance_en: How a deputy prime minister who also heads a ministry is introduced.

phrases.en: The deputy prime minister spoke first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직책 뒤에 '-님'을 붙여 높여 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -님 to the title is the polite way to refer to or address the person.

explain_en: In Korea a deputy prime minister often also serves as the minister of a ministry such as the economy or education. In the news you hear it with the field in front, like '경제부총리'.
